newsitem.title: USA: NY Governor vetoes Westchester's property tax bill.
newsitem.headline: NY Governor vetoes Westchester's property tax bill.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki has vetoed legislation that he said would have allowed Westchester County to use a markedly different system for assessing and taxing real property.
Under the bill that Pataki vetoed on Friday, Westchester could have taxed real property according to three different classes.

The first class would have included one-, two- and three- family parcels and condominiums, while the second would have included all other residential real property and cooperative apartments. The third class of property would have covered all other property, from farmlands to small businesses.

While all real property would have been valued at full market value, each assessing unit could have adopted different tax rates. In contrast, current law requires that all property in Weschester be valued at a uniform percentage of its value and taxed at the same rate.

Pataki applauded the bill's effort to use full-market valuation, saying this helps residents determine if they are paying their fair share of taxes compared with their neighbors. And he noted high property taxes are a problem in Westchester.
But he said the bill might be unconstitutional, as it would limit the rights of citizens to get assessments reviewed, and discriminate against cooperative apartments.
Further, he said the new bill would seriously hurt small businesses.
